Article Title: Love, the thief of sleep
Article Text:
Naadi Josiyar

Naadi Jothidam

“Ya Devi Sarva Bhuteshu Nidra Rupena Samsthita”

Kama Kadumpunal Neendhi KaraiKaanane

Yaamaththum Yaane Ulene.

“I cannot swim across the terrible sea of love, as I am sleepless all night”

Dear sleep, be kind to this little soul. Let night hold him gently, and give him, at last, the peace he has been longing for.

Most of my batchmates live in the US. When they visit Chennai, they sometimes reach out for help—hiring cabs, visiting temples etc. Sampath, a dear friend, has never asked for any such favour. He meticulously plans his annual trips.So, his request this time was unusual.He wanted me to find a reliablenear Vaitheeswaran Koil. I knew little about—the belief that ancient sages foresaw and recorded the past, present and future lives of people on dried palm leaves.Sampath arrived with his wife and son Shreyas. All of them looked pale and worn out. Shreyas was every NRI parent’s dream: brilliant grades, spelling-bee trophies, Carnatic music, Indian values, respect for grandparents, admissions in top medical schools.What, then, was the need for aI made a few calls, found the address and arranged their travel. Later that night, we travelled back by train. I sleep poorly in trains. Each time I woke, I saw Shreyas staring at his phone. He climbed down from his berth and back up countless times. Once, I thought I saw him crying.The next day, we parted. The same evening, Sampath came home and poured his heart out. A girl in Shreyas’ class had first sought his help with studies and then declared her love . Shreyas, reserved and inexperienced, slowly fell completely in love. For two years, he gave himself to the relationship; coaching her for medical entrance exams, waiting outside her home with her favourite food and flowers. His family welcomed her as one of their own.Then, one day, she simply announced a breakup, through a text.For the last six months, Shreyas had barely slept. Therapy, medication, and repeated attempts to meet her brought no results.Finally, Sampath brought him to India—and to theTheapparently said he would be betrayed by a girl. It promised him a bright future and marriage after seven years.Sampath was unmoved. “Forget his marriage and medical admission. I want my son to sleep.”I remembered the young boy staring at his phone in the train.Yes, if he could sleep, perhaps he could come out of this agony—the agony of rejection, betrayal and not knowing where he had failed.Perhaps men and women process heartbreak differently; but young men, especially when love is new, can surrender themselves to it with intensity.“What greater sorrow can engulf a parent than seeing a child suffer like this?”Sampath cried.I told him his son’s love was pure. Like all pure things, it would be put to test. He was going to become someone who would give the gift of life to humanity. He had no reason to feel purposeless.After Sampath left, I thought of the—the Devi who dwells in all beings as sleep.And then I remembered Thiruvalluvar:Night is not merely the absence of day. She is her gentler twin—the quiet Devi who gathers the wounded, the betrayed and the lonely into her embrace.
Article Summary: Sampath, a dear friend, has never asked for any such favour. He wanted me to find a reliablenear Vaitheeswaran Koil. For the last six months, Shreyas had barely slept. Therapy, medication, and repeated attempts to meet her brought no results.

Article Title: LeBron James’ son Bronny James gets career threat warning ahead of new NBA season as his father departed from Lakers
Article Text:
Bronny James gets fresh warning over his future with the Lakers. Image via: Juan Ocampo/NBAE via Getty Images

Bronny James gets Lakers future warning

Bronny James understands his role with the Lakers

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Bronny James made it through the wildest offseason of his young career without losing his roster spot. His future in the purple and gold has been in question after his father, LeBron James , decided to leave the roster to join the Philadelphia 76ers.The guard now finds himself squeezed for minutes after the Lakers rebuild their roster and LeBron James left the franchise behind. The clock on proving himself is ticking louder than ever heading into 2026-27.Nothing suggests Bronny James is getting traded or waived any time soon. But the runway is shorter than it looked a year ago, and the Lakers' front office has made that much clear through their offseason moves.Jacob Rude of Silver Screen and Roll captured the mood surrounding Bronny's situation, writing that the Lakers have shown patience with his growth but are starting to expect more from him. In Rude's words, “As much as he has shown signs of progress, though, the time has come for him to be more than a project and to make good on the team’s investment in him.”His contract is fully guaranteed for next season, so there's no financial reason for Los Angeles to move on early.He also made it through the roster shakeup that claimed several other spots. For now, he's expected to report to training camp with the team.Still, the Lakers have to trim their roster before the season tips off, which puts real weight on how Bronny performs in the coming weeks. A starting job isn't realistic. Even a bigger bench role looks tough given how crowded the backcourt has become with new additions.Bronny isn't pretending the picture is simple. Asked what part of his game needed the most work, he laid out a wide list of goals rather than picking one lane. He needs to be a threat off the ball playing alongside Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves, and he knows scoring is part of that."I need to be able to knock down shots and create for others," Bronny recently said, describing where his focus lies this season.Los Angeles is currently carrying 16 players for 15 spots, and most signs point to Jarred Vanderbilt, Dalton Knecht, or Jaden Hardy as the likely cut, not Bronny. The date that would have let the Lakers save money by releasing him has already passed, which suggests they want one more year to watch him grow.The Lakers hold a team option on the final year of his deal, meaning they could move on next summer without any cap consequences. Whatever role he claims over the next several months will likely decide whether Los Angeles keeps betting on him or lets him go.
Article Summary: Bronny James is expected to report to training camp with the Lakers. His future in the purple and gold has been in question after his father, LeBron James, left. The clock on proving himself is ticking louder than ever heading into 2026-27.

Article Title: Could Josue De Paula be the unexpected answer for Los Angeles Dodgers after Shohei Ohtani’s injury changed everything?
Article Text:
Josue De Paula steps into the spotlight for his long-awaited MLB opportunity (Image via IG/X)

Josue De Paula became the unexpected Los Angeles Dodgers answer when Shohei Ohtani’s injury created a sudden opening

Shohei Ohtani’s absence gives Josue De Paula a chance to make his mark

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Josue De Paula thought he was heading to Triple-A when Eric Wedge told him he was getting called up. Instead, the Los Angeles Dodgers prospect learned he was going straight to the major leagues. The surprise became even bigger when Josue De Paula found out he would make his MLB debut as the designated hitter while Shohei Ohtani was sidelined. At only 21, Josue De Paula suddenly found himself with an important opportunity during the final days of the regular season. It was not the path he expected, but the Dodgers needed another bat, and Josue De Paula was ready to see what he could do.The reason Josue De Paula suddenly became an option for the Los Angeles Dodgers was Shohei Ohtani’s injury. The Dodgers placed Shohei Ohtani on the injured list with right biceps inflammation, creating an opening at designated hitter during an important part of the season.But Josue De Paula did not know that opportunity was coming.The news arrived after Josue De Paula finished another strong performance with Double-A Tulsa. When Eric Wedge told him he was being promoted, Josue De Paula initially assumed the next stop would be Triple-A.His reaction showed just how unexpected the news was.“Literally, I was like, ‘What? Going up where?’” Josue De Paula said with a laugh.Eric Wedge quickly gave him the answer.“He’s like, ‘You’re going with the big dogs.’”Josue De Paula was stunned. A direct jump from Double-A to the major leagues was not what he had pictured, especially with the regular season nearly finished.“No way,” Josue De Paula thought.The timing made the moment even harder to believe. Josue De Paula had only four games remaining with his minor league club and was already thinking about finishing the season before heading home.“I always had it in the back of my mind that it could happen [this year],” Josue De Paula said. “But when it did happen, I wasn’t really expecting it because we only had four games to go in the season. So I was thinking four days, playoffs, then home.”Instead, Josue De Paula was heading to Miami for his first major league appearance.“To be honest, no,” Josue De Paula said when asked whether he had even considered getting called up directly from Double-A. “It took me off guard. But when it happened, I was so happy.”The sudden promotion gave Josue De Paula a chance to show the Los Angeles Dodgers what he could bring at the highest level.Shohei Ohtani’s absence became official when the Los Angeles Dodgers placed him on the injured list. The move was backdated to Tuesday, meaning Shohei Ohtani is not eligible to return until Sept. 23.That absence created an opening at designated hitter, and the Los Angeles Dodgers quickly turned to Josue De Paula.The plan was for Josue De Paula to receive three consecutive starts against the Miami Marlins. That gives the 21-year-old an immediate chance to adjust to major league pitching while helping a Dodgers lineup dealing with several important absences.Josue De Paula knows the opportunity is significant, but he does not appear interested in changing his entire approach simply because the competition has become tougher.“[I want to show them] just what I’m about,” Josue De Paula said. “Nothing I feel I really have to change, especially on the offensive side. Just do what I know how to do. At the end of the day, I love competing.”That approach could be valuable for the Los Angeles Dodgers. Josue De Paula is not being asked to become Shohei Ohtani overnight. Instead, the young prospect has a chance to provide another offensive option while showing whether his production in the minors can carry over to the major leagues.The Dodgers are also entering a crucial part of the season, making every at-bat more important. With Shohei Ohtani unavailable, the club needs other hitters to step forward and keep the lineup productive.For Josue De Paula, the opportunity arrived almost without warning. One moment, he was preparing to finish his Double-A season. Days later, he was standing in a major league lineup.The question now is whether Josue De Paula can turn an unexpected promotion into a lasting impression for the Los Angeles Dodgers.
Article Summary: Josue De Paula thought he was heading to Triple-A when Eric Wedge told him he was getting called up. The Los Angeles Dodgers placed Shohei Ohtani on the injured list, creating an opening at designated hitter. The 21-year-old will receive three consecutive starts against the Miami Marlins.

Article Title: “It’s huge for me, it means standing alongside women”: How Angel Reese is building a global sports empire through major ownership moves beyond the WNBA
Article Text:
How Angel Reese is building a global sports empire through major ownership moves beyond the WNBA(Getty Images)

Angel Reese adds Brisbane Bullets ownership to her growing sports portfolio

From DC Power FC to TOGETHXR , Angel Reese keeps building beyond basketball

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Angel Reese is building a name for herself far beyond the basketball court. The WNBA star has already stepped into sports ownership in the US, and her latest move has taken that business journey overseas.In March 2026, Reese joined the ownership group of the Brisbane Bullets in Australia. The move added professional basketball in another country to a growing portfolio that includes soccer and women’s sports media.The Brisbane Bullets announced on March 10, 2026, that Reese had joined the club’s ownership group. She joined majority owner Jason Levien and co-owner Ben Haan, with the group also pursuing a new WNBL team in Brisbane.That makes the deal more than a simple investment for Reese. The Brisbane Bullets compete in Australia’s National Basketball League, while the ownership group has also been working toward bringing a women’s team to the city through a bid for the WNBL’s 10th license.The move also followed Reese’s visit to Australia with Reebok. She promoted new colorways of her Angel Reese 1 signature shoe during the trip. Reebok also announced a footwear partnership with the WNBL that will begin in 2027.Brisbane Bullets CEO Malcolm Watts welcomed Reese to the group and highlighted what her profile could bring to basketball in Queensland.“Angel is a fantastic ambassador for basketball and a globally recognised superstar,” Watts said in the Bullets’ announcement. He also pointed to basketball’s growth in Queensland and the message Reese can send to young players in Brisbane.The Bullets also announced Will Weaver as their president of basketball operations and head coach on March 10, giving the organization another major change around the same time Reese joined its ownership group.The Brisbane investment follows two earlier ownership moves. Reese joined the ownership group of DC Power FC in 2024, giving her a stake in professional soccer while she continued her WNBA career.Then, in September 2025, she joined the ownership group of TOGETHXR, the sports media and lifestyle company founded by Sue Bird, Alex Morgan, Simone Manuel and Chloe Kim.Reese explained what the opportunity meant to her while explaining what it meant for her:“It’s huge for me,” Reese said. “It means standing alongside women who aren’t just legends in their sports, but real trailblazers in business and culture. They’ve opened doors for so many of us, and now I get to lock arms with them and keep pushing things forward.”She also explained that she wanted to bring her own perspective to the established group rather than simply step into someone else’s role.“It’s not so much about teaching them as it is about joining them, and bringing a fresh perspective into everything they’ve already been doing so well,” Reese told USA TODAY Sports in the same interview.Her business work also connects with her foundation. Reese founded the Angel C. Reese Foundation in 2023, with a focus on empowering girls and women through sports, education and financial literacy.Now, the Brisbane Bullets give Reese another link to the sports business world, this time outside the United States. Now she remains a key player for Atlanta Dream but her growing ownership portfolio shows that she is already building opportunities beyond her WNBA career.At 24, Reese has moved into soccer, sports media and international basketball while continuing to develop her own brand. The Brisbane deal adds another major piece to that picture.
Article Summary: Angel Reese adds Brisbane Bullets ownership to her growing sports portfolio. The WNBA star has already stepped into sports ownership in the US, and her latest move has taken that business journey overseas. Reese joined the ownership group of DC Power FC in 2024, giving her a stake in professional soccer while she continued her WNBA career.

Dallas has spent the entire offseason swatting away calls about Kyrie Irving , and that stance hasn't wavered. But the questions keep coming, and they're not going away just because the front office says no in June.The nine-time All-Star is 34, playing next to a 19-year-old Cooper Flagg, and locked into a contract that runs through at least 2026-27. That combination alone is enough to keep rival executives calling. If Dallas stumbles out of the gate this season, the Heat are reportedly one of the teams ready to move.Marc Stein has been writing about this since mid-June, and the core tension hasn't changed: Dallas keeps saying no, but nobody around the league is convinced that holds if the Mavericks struggle early. The February 11 trade deadline is the pressure point everyone's watching. Stein pointed to the roster's age gap as the real driver of the speculation, "Rival teams, however, continue to wonder aloud about how firmly Dallas will stick to that stance once the season begins and the next in-season trade deadline on Feb. 11 gradually approaches. The primary factor fueling that curiosity, of course, is that fact that Irving is 34 and Mavericks star forward Cooper Flagg is 19.Not your average age gap between the team's two best players," Stein wrote.Heat RoundTable's Sean Jordan has gone further, reporting that Kyrie Irving, who has made a stunning $347 million in his career so far, has been included in trade discussions throughout the entire offseason, with Miami still in the mix even after an active summer of its own. If Dallas's stance softens once games start counting, Jordan's reporting suggests the Heat won't need much time to make a call.Jordan's reporting names Andrew Wiggins and Nikola Jovic as the two outgoing pieces most likely to headline a Heat offer. Wiggins gives Dallas size and two-way length on the wing, while Jovic adds a younger frontcourt option still on his rookie-scale value.This wouldn't be Miami's first blockbuster of the year. The Heat already reshaped their roster once, acquiring Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis from Milwaukee for a package built around Tyler Herro. As ESPN's Shams Charania previously reported, the Bucks agreed to a deal trading franchise icon Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis to the Miami Heat for Herro, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakucionis, three first-round picks, a pick swap, and a second-rounder.Adding Irving to a roster that already includes Antetokounmpo would give Pat Riley's front office one of the most talented cores in the league, built through two separate win-now trades inside the same calendar year.The two players' most recent numbers aren't from the same season. Irving didn't play last season, so his stat line below reflects 2024-25, his last full year on the floor, while Wiggins' numbers are from 2025-26 with Miami.Irving's last healthy season shows a clear scoring and playmaking gap over Wiggins, and pairing him with Antetokounmpo would make Miami a genuine contender on paper. The catch is that none of this moves until Dallas actually blinks, and right now, the Mavericks aren't blinking.
Article Summary: Dallas has spent the entire offseason swatting away calls about Kyrie Irving. If Dallas stumbles out of the gate this season, the Heat are reportedly one of the teams ready to move. Andrew Wiggins and Nikola Jovic are the two outgoing pieces most likely to headline a Heat offer.

Article Title: Why is Josh Jacobs’ Packers future suddenly uncertain? The RB’s legal trouble puts Matt LaFleur in a difficult spot
Article Text:
Why is Josh Jacobs’ Packers future suddenly uncertain? The RB’s legal trouble puts Matt LaFleur in a difficult spot(Image via getty Images)

Why is Matt LaFleur standing by Josh Jacobs despite the legal case?

Could Josh Jacobs still miss games despite his no-contest plea?

Josh Jacobs’ future with the Green Bay Packers has taken another turn. The running back pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges in Wisconsin on Thursday, September 10, but Matt LaFleur says his view of Jacobs has not changed.The Packers coach also made it clear that the team will wait for the NFL to finish its investigation before making any decision about Jacobs. For now, the 28-year-old remains on the Commissioner’s Exempt List and cannot play or practice.LaFleur addressed Jacobs’ situation ahead of the Packers’ season opener against the Minnesota Vikings. When reporters asked whether his opinion of Jacobs had changed, the Packers coach gave a blunt answer.“No,” LaFleur said while speaking to reporters. He then pointed to his relationship with Jacobs and his view of the running back’s character.“I know the guy, and I know the character of the guy. … Unfortunately, situations occur in life, and it’s just an unfortunate situation.”LaFleur did not stop there. When reporters asked why Green Bay would keep Jacobs on the roster if he is found guilty, he refused to speculate.“I’m not gonna get into any of this until the league completes their investigation,” LaFleur said during the same media session.That leaves the Packers in a holding pattern. Green Bay has not released Jacobs, while general manager Brian Gutekunst also said the team hopes he can play this season.“I think that’s to be seen,” Gutekunst said while discussing Jacobs’ 2026 status. “Certainly hopeful that he will, and certainly would expect that, but we’re gonna let that process play out.”Jacobs pleaded no contest on September 10 to misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property charges. The agreement gave him a $1,000 fine and court-ordered conditions for the battery charges. The criminal-damage charge received a 12-month deferred disposition and could get dismissed if Jacobs meets the conditions.Those conditions include avoiding contact with the victim, attending counseling, paying restitution and staying out of trouble. Jacobs also remains under criminal-justice supervision.“I fully understand the seriousness of the situation and I take full responsibility,” Jacobs said, per ESPN, following the plea.However, the end of the criminal case does not end the NFL’s review. The league placed Jacobs on the Commissioner’s Exempt List in August while it investigates under its personal-conduct policy.The NFL confirmed on September 10 that there had been no change to Jacobs’ status. He cannot practice or play, although he can receive his salary and use team facilities with Green Bay’s permission.Jacobs was arrested on May 26 after police investigated a disturbance involving him and his girlfriend at his Wisconsin home. Prosecutors later filed only the two misdemeanor charges.Now, the NFL has the next call. A suspension remains possible, but the league has not announced one. Therefore, despite LaFleur’s public support, Josh Jacobs’ 2026 season still depends on the outcome of the NFL investigation.
Article Summary: Josh Jacobs pleaded no contest to misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property charges on September 10. Green Bay Packers coach Matt LaFleur says his view of Jacobs has not changed. The NFL is still investigating Jacobs' case and has not announced a suspension.

Article Title: Cristiano Ronaldo listed his 23-acre Cheshire estate with a 7-bedroom mansion for $7.4 million; after more than 18 months on the market, it fell to $6.7 million
Article Text:
Cristiano Ronaldo listed his 23-acre Cheshire estate with a 7-bedroom mansion for $7.4 million; after more than 18 months on the market, it fell to $6.7 million

What does Cristiano Ronaldo’s 23-acre Cheshire estate include

Why did Cristiano Ronaldo leave the Cheshire mansion after returning to Manchester United

Why was Cristiano Ronaldo’s Cheshire estate listed for sale in 2023

Why did Cristiano Ronaldo’s property price fall to $6.7 million

$6.7 million

How did Cristiano Ronaldo’s earlier Cheshire home perform when he sold it

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Cristiano Ronaldo’s former Cheshire estate was listed for about $7.4 million in 2023, but the asking price was later reduced to around $6.7 million after the property struggled to find a buyer. The huge estate in Alderley Edge covers 23 acres and includes a seven-bedroom mansion, six bathrooms, an indoor heated pool, gym, sauna, jacuzzi and cinema. There are also tennis and padel courts and a separate two-bedroom guest barn. Ronaldo moved into the property after returning to Manchester United in 2021, but his family soon moved to another Cheshire home. The estate was later put up for sale after his move to Saudi Arabia.Ronaldo’s former Cheshire home is built on a scale that goes well beyond a typical luxury house. The estate covers 23 acres in Alderley Edge, one of the well-known wealthy areas in Cheshire, while the main mansion has seven bedrooms and six bathrooms.The house was designed with both family life and fitness in mind. The main bedroom has private dressing areas and walk-in wardrobe space, while the other bedrooms have en-suite facilities.A large leisure area is one of the biggest features of the property. It has an indoor heated swimming pool, sauna and jacuzzi, along with a professional gym. For entertainment, there is a private cinema room and a wine cellar.The outdoor space adds even more to the property. Ronaldo’s former estate has a full-sized tennis court and a padel court, giving the owner options for sport without leaving the grounds.There is also a separate two-bedroom guest barn. It provides additional space for visitors, staff or security personnel while keeping the main house private.When Jackson-Stops listed the property, the estate agency described it as a “masterpiece of modern design set in 23 acres - an ultra stylish main residence with superb leisure suite, two bedroom guest barn and padel court.”Ronaldo did not stay in the mansion for long after returning to Manchester United in 2021. He and his family moved out soon after arriving in the area and shifted to another property in Cheshire.One explanation that appeared in reports at the time involved the land around the house. The estate bordered open farmland, and early-morning noise from sheep was said to have been a problem for Ronaldo.However, that detail has been disputed and should not be treated as the confirmed reason for the move. Privacy and security were also reported as concerns, especially because a public footpath ran close to the property.For someone as well known as Ronaldo, having people regularly passing near the estate could make privacy harder to maintain. His family therefore moved to another Cheshire property that had previously been owned by former Manchester United striker Andrew Cole.That home offered stronger security measures, including electric gates and CCTV, making it a better fit for the family.Ronaldo’s second Manchester United spell ended in November 2022 after his contract was terminated by mutual consent. The decision followed his high-profile television interview with Piers Morgan, in which he openly criticized the club and its leadership.A few weeks later, Ronaldo began the next stage of his career in Saudi Arabia after signing for Al-Nassr. That move also changed where he and his family spent most of their time.With Ronaldo no longer playing in Manchester, keeping a 23-acre estate in Cheshire made less sense. The property had already not been his family’s main home during the latter part of his United spell.Jackson-Stops placed the estate on the market in February 2023 with an asking price of £5.5 million, which was about $7.4 million based on the conversion used for the listing.The sale came as Ronaldo’s property holdings continued to stretch across several countries. Rather than keeping a large home in northern England that he was no longer using, the Cheshire estate became a property he could sell.Finding a buyer for a property of this size can take time. Ronaldo’s Cheshire estate remained on the market for more than 18 months, and the asking price was eventually reduced by £500,000.The new guide price was £5 million, or aboutThe reduction does not mean the property was sold for $6.7 million. It was the lower asking price after the original listing failed to attract a buyer within the expected period.There are practical reasons why a property like this can take longer to sell. The estate has 23 acres of land, which means a buyer is taking on much more than the upkeep of a normal house. The mansion also has a long list of specialist facilities, including an indoor pool, gym, tennis court and padel court.Those features can be attractive to the right buyer, but they can also make the property more expensive and demanding to maintain.The price cut also stands out because Ronaldo has previously experienced a difficult sale in the same area.Ronaldo owned another house in Alderley Edge during his first Manchester United spell. That property was a five-bedroom brick house with luxury facilities, including an indoor swimming pool and gym.He bought the earlier property in 2008 for a reported £3.895 million. It was eventually sold in 2019 for £3.25 million, meaning the sale price was around £645,000 lower than what he had originally paid.That house and the current 23-acre estate are different properties, but both show that even a famous footballer’s luxury home can take time to sell.The current estate was bought around Ronaldo’s return to Manchester United and later became unnecessary after his career moved away from England. Its large size and unusual collection of facilities also put it into a small section of the property market.For now, the important change is the asking price. Cristiano Ronaldo’s former seven-bedroom Cheshire estate went from about $7.4 million to $6.7 million, but a final sale price has not been confirmed.
Article Summary: Cristiano Ronaldo listed his 23-acre Cheshire estate with a 7-bedroom mansion for $7.4 million in 2023. The asking price was later reduced to around $6.7 million after the property struggled to find a buyer. Ronaldo moved into the property after returning to Manchester United in 2021, but his family soon moved to another Cheshire home. The estate was later put up for sale after his move to Saudi Arabia.

Article Title: How Aryna Sabalenka’s fiancé Georgios Frangulis built his own empire before becoming her biggest supporter
Article Text:
Georgios Frangulis and Aryna Sabalenka (Getty Images)

Who is Georgios Frangulis, Aryna Sabalenka 's fiancé?

Aryna Sabalenka and Georgios Frangulis (Getty Images)

How did Georgios Frangulis build Oakberry into a global brand?

When did Aryna Sabalenka and Georgios Frangulis start dating?

How did Georgios Frangulis propose to Aryna Sabalenka?

What is 'The Gride,' Georgios Frangulis's new fashion brand?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Long before he was cheering from the players' box at Grand Slams, Georgios Frangulis was building something of his own. The Brazilian entrepreneur dropped out of law school, founded an açaí brand called Oakberry in 2016, and grew it into a global business with more than 800 stores across 50 countries. Now 37, Frangulis proposed to world No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka in March 2026, capping a relationship that began when she signed on as an Oakberry brand ambassador in early 2024.Born and raised in São Paulo, Brazil, Frangulis has Greek roots, with his family originally from Thessaloniki, Greece. He studied law at FAAP -- Fundação Armando Alvares Penteado -- in 2014, but never sat the bar exam."I always knew I wouldn't be a lawyer," he said. "What I really wanted was to be an entrepreneur."That clarity of purpose was rare at the time. Most people spend years hedging. Frangulis walked away from a law degree, moved to the United States, where he became infatuated with açaí, came back to São Paulo, and launched Oakberry in December 2016.Co-founded alongside Renato Haidar, Oakberry was not just another smoothie shop. Frangulis positioned açaí as functional nutrition -- clean ingredients, no artificial syrups, and a strong link to fitness culture -- and built a franchise model designed from day one to scale internationally.The company raised $67 million in capital in late 2023. By mid-2026, Oakberry had grown to a 900-location global business, with stores in Dubai malls, Miami gyms, Australian beach towns, and European city centres -- all without compromising brand consistency.In June 2023, Frangulis graced the cover of Forbes Brazil. The profile explored not just his entrepreneurial arc but his spirituality and Greek identity. His bicep tattoo reads "Fight for us, Saint George the Warrior." His forearm reads, "The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want." These are not the accessories of a brand persona.His net worth in 2026 is estimated between $75 million and $100 million -- built almost entirely from his equity in Oakberry, not from market listings or quick exits.They met in January 2024 when Sabalenka was hired as an ambassador for Oakberry. The couple were first spotted together in April 2024 -- a month after the tragic and untimely death of Sabalenka's ex-boyfriend, Konstantin Koltsov, who died by suicide in March 2024.It was a difficult period, and Sabalenka has been open about what Frangulis meant to her during it. "There was a really tough period where I was really happy to have him by my side, always cheering me up, always making sure that we are doing some fun stuff," she told People. "His support means so much to me. Being on the road and having him support me, to make me laugh and to be able to work out together, makes life on the road feel more like home. "Sabalenka had been broadly hinting for months. After winning the Brisbane International in January 2026, she said in her victory speech: "Thank you to my boyfriend... Hopefully soon I can call you something else, right? Let's just put some extra pressure."Frangulis proposed to Sabalenka in Indian Wells, California, on March 3, 2026. The setting was candlelit, with rose petals arranged beside a pool -- a rental home the couple had spent time in since the early days of their relationship. Sabalenka, in jeans and a white t-shirt, had no idea it was coming."I always knew I wanted to propose to Aryna because I was 100% sure she was the person I wanted to spend the rest of my life with," he shared in a YouTube video about the moment.The ring was designed by Isabela Grutman, who worked with Frangulis for months to create the custom piece. It features a 12-carat, oval-cut diamond surrounded by emeralds set in platinum -- Sabalenka's favorite stone, and also her birthstone. Experts told InStyle the ring could be worth up to $1 million. They captioned their joint Instagram post: "You & me, forever."Earlier in 2026, Frangulis launched his own fashion brand, named The Gride. The name honors his Greek heritage and mixes the words Greek and Pride. "My pride comes from my grandparents and has spread to my closest circle," the brand's website states. "The feeling is unmatched, and I'll do my best to make each and every one of you feel it too."Outside business, Frangulis races Porsche GT3 Cup cars. "Getting in the car and racing is one of the few moments when nothing else matters," he told Forbes Brazil. For someone whose professional life spans dozens of countries and time zones, that says something about how he recharges.What is clear is that Frangulis arrived in this relationship with his own story already written. He built a global company from a fruit most of the world had never heard of, then quietly showed up for the woman he loves at every stop on the tour. That is not a supporting role. It is just a different kind of ambition.
Article Summary: Georgios Frangulis proposed to world No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka in March 2026. The Brazilian entrepreneur dropped out of law school, founded an açaí brand called Oakberry in 2016, and grew it into a global business. He is estimated to be worth between $75 million and $100 million.

Article Title: “I’m proud to support each of these organizations”: How Caitlin Clark honored Iowa with four $22,000 grants, including one inspired by her private hospital visits

How Caitlin Clark honored Iowa with four $22,000 grants, including one inspired by her private hospital visits (Image via Getty: Caitlin Clark)

Caitlin Clark turned personal Iowa memories into four $22,000 grants

Caitlin Clark wanted her Iowa connection to continue

Caitlin Clark’s Iowa journey gave her some of the biggest moments of her basketball career, but the community also gave her memories that had little to do with scoring records or packed arenas. During her time with the Hawkeyes, Clark built personal connections with several Iowa organizations, including the University of Iowa Children’s Hospital, where she regularly spent time with young patients and their families.Ahead of her No. 22 jersey retirement in February 2025, Clark found a personal way to give back. Her foundation announced four $22,000 grants to Iowa organizations that had made an impact on her during her college years. The donations showed that Clark wanted her Iowa legacy to include the people and communities who had supported her away from the basketball court.The idea for the four grants came directly from CaitlinClark in the weeks leading up to her jersey retirement. According to the Caitlin Clark Foundation, she called home and asked how she could give back in a way that felt meaningful and personal. She wanted to recognize the Iowa community that had supported her throughout her college career, and the four organizations she selected each carried a different connection to her journey.The University of Iowa Children’s Hospital received one of the $22,000 grants, and that donation had a particularly personal connection. Clark had made regular, often private visits to the hospital during her years as a student-athlete. She met young patients and their families, offering them encouragement during difficult moments. However, the Foundation said Clark often walked away from those visits feeling just as encouraged and inspired by the children she had met.Those visits became some of Clark’s most cherished experiences away from basketball. That makes the grant more than another charitable contribution connected to her name. It reflected a relationship she had developed during her time in Iowa City and the impression those young patients had left on her.The other three recipients also had meaningful links to Caitlin Clark. She had personally supported the Boys and Girls Club of the Corridor earlier in her career and understood how important it was for children to have a safe and encouraging place to learn and grow. Special Olympics Iowa-East Central became another important connection through Clark’s friendship and mentorship with Debbie Antonelli, whose work with Special Olympics inspired her involvement.The Coralville Community Food Pantry held an even earlier connection. It was where Clark began her own journey of giving back, learning through those experiences that something as simple as helping provide a meal could make a difference in someone’s day and potentially their future.Caitlin Clark made it clear that her relationship with Iowa City was about more than the years she spent wearing an Iowa jersey. She wanted to remain connected to the community that had supported her as her career continued to grow.“One of my favorite things about Iowa City is the way the community is connected and how everyone supports each other,” Clark said. “It’s something I felt deeply during my time here, and it’s something I want to stay connected with for the rest of my life.”The WNBA star also shared a simple message about the organizations receiving the grants.“I’m proud to support each of these organizations and the meaningful impact they make for the people of Iowa,” Clark said.Caitlin Clark Foundation president Mary Coffin also highlighted the impact behind Clark’s involvement, saying, “Caitlin is an example for all of us on the impact one interaction can have and the legacy of uplifting others.”The four grants were announced on Jan, 2025, only days before Iowa retired Clark’s No. 22 jersey. While that ceremony celebrated her remarkable career on the court, the grants offered another look at the legacy she was building away from basketball, especially through the private moments she shared with the Iowa community.
Article Summary: Caitlin Clark wanted to recognize the Iowa community that had supported her throughout her college career. Her foundation announced four $22,000 grants to Iowa organizations that had made an impact on her during her college years. The University of Iowa Children’s Hospital received one of the grants, and that donation had a particularly personal connection.

Ben Shelton net worth talk has picked up pace after his stunning five-set win over Carlos Alcaraz sent him into a US Open semifinal against fellow American Frances Tiafoe. The 23-year-old closed out the deciding tie-break with an ace in the tournament's latest finish on record.The victory also reshaped the discussion around his earnings. Shelton and Tiafoe carry different career prize-money totals into their all-American semifinal, and only one of them has a confirmed net worth figure, a gap that has become part of the story heading into Friday's meeting. His career prize money has surpassed $13.3 million, with more than $1.8 million of that coming during the current season alone, fueled by Grand Slam performances including semifinal appearances at the 2023 US Open and 2025 Australian Open.Separately, current tour figures put Shelton's total career prize money at $15.06 million across a 144-90 record, reflecting his four titles this year in Dallas, Munich and Stuttgart and a climb as high as World No.5. Beyond the court, Shelton has built out a commercial portfolio with Rolex, On Running, Yonex, Loewe, Ralph Lauren, Thorne Health and Bose, and added visibility through Netflix's Break Point and his own YouTube series.Frances Tiafoe's net worth is estimated at $8 million, according to Celebrity Net Worth. The 28-year-old has built that fortune over more than a decade on tour, since making his ATP debut at 16 with a wildcard into the 2014 Citi Open. He broke into the world's top 100 by the end of 2017 and reached his first major breakthrough at the 2022 US Open, upsetting Rafael Nadal on his way to the semifinals.Tiafoe's career prize money has grown from just over $6 million heading into that 2022 run to more than $20.15 million by this year's US Open, after his quarterfinal win over Alex Michelsen added another $1.45 million. Forbes estimated his total earnings at $15.2 million for the 12 months ending in August 2025, with $12 million of that coming from endorsements, appearances and exhibitions rather than prize money.Sponsorship has played a major role in that growth. It was Shelton's first win in 18 tries against a top-three opponent and ended Alcaraz's 18-match Grand Slam winning streak.Alcaraz was visibly unwell during the match, sick into his towel at one stage, and neither man was broken in the deciding set. Shelton credited the crowd that stayed through a match that ran past 3 a.m., before turning his attention to his opponent. "Sharing the court with Carlos is an absolute honor," he said.That result now sets up an all-American semifinal where Shelton's history against Tiafoe, and his surging form, will meet Tiafoe's deeper reserve of career earnings and a chance to settle which of the two owns the bigger 2026 breakthrough.

Article Title: How Ben Shelton and Trinity Rodman turned red-eye flights and conflicting schedules into the unlikely foundation of a winning relationship
Article Text:
Ben Shelton and Trinity Rodman (Getty Images)

How did Ben Shelton and Trinity Rodman start dating?

How do Ben Shelton and Trinity Rodman manage their schedules?

Ben Shelton and Trinity Rodman love stroy (Getty Images)

Why does Ben Shelton say having Trinity Rodman as a partner matters?

How has Trinity Rodman supported Ben Shelton publicly?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

What makes their relationship different from other sports couples?

Tennis star Ben Shelton is having the best year of his career. He is in the US Open semi-finals, ranked No. 9 in the world, and has already collected titles in Montreal, Munich, Dallas, and Stuttgart in 2026. Behind that run is a partnership with Washington Spirit forward and two-time Olympic gold medalist Trinity Rodman that has grown as fast as his ranking. What makes it interesting is not the romance itself, but the specific, unglamorous lengths both have gone to for each other when their schedules collide.Rodman made the first move, sending Shelton an Instagram DM that simply said "You're sick," accompanied by a fire emoji. Shelton replied within ten minutes, telling her she had been "sick at the Olympics too." They met in person a week or two later, and by March 2025, they had made the relationship Instagram official.Rodman later called the whole thing "cringe" on a podcast. Speaking on the *Not Gonna Lie* podcast with Kylie Kelce, she laughed it off: "Everything I do is just embarrassing. I'm really embarrassed. I said 'You're sick, fire emoji'. That's it. It worked... he responded within 10 minutes, so I win!"What came next was less funny and more telling. "I fully committed to this guy that I didn't even meet yet, for him to stay at my house for the weekend," Rodman said."It's actually crazy, it's insane, but it worked out." That willingness to just figure things out on the fly has become something of a theme for them.This is where most sports couples hit a wall. Two elite athletes, two separate leagues, two travel-heavy calendars with almost no natural overlap. Rodman plays for the Washington Spirit in the NWSL and represents the US Women's National Team. Shelton chases ATP ranking points across multiple continents from January to November. The math rarely works.But they make it work anyway. At the 2025 US Open, Shelton told the crowd during his on-court interview: "My girlfriend took the red-eye from California last night to be here." Less than a day earlier, Rodman had been on the opposite side of the country, playing for the Spirit against Bay FC. By the following afternoon, she was sitting with Shelton's family in New York.It is easy to gloss over how much effort that actually takes. She played a professional match, boarded an overnight flight, landed at 5am, and was sitting courtside before noon. Shelton noticed. He said afterwards: "2 days off. I have some free time. My girlfriend took the red-eye from California last night to be here." The crowd roared. But what stuck was the simplicity of it. No grand gesture, no social media build-up. She just showed up.Shelton has returned the favour in kind. After his first-round exit from Wimbledon in July 2026, he was soon back in the stands watching Rodman play for the Spirit. She scored a 94th-minute winner against Houston, then ran toward the stands to celebrate with Shelton with a kiss. One week down, the next one up. That rhythm is the relationship.Shelton has been clear that what he values most is not the presence, but the understanding behind it. He told the ATP Tour: "It's very important I think, one, having my family in my corner, who have been super supportive my whole career, it's really important. And, two, having a partner, a girlfriend, who understands all the same things, knows when to support, what to say in tough moments — is selfless enough to be there for me in my moments and actually enjoy my big moments and vice versa — has been really cool. "That word, selfless, keeps coming up. He told Us Weekly: "You gotta make sacrifices sometimes. It's just the life that we live. I think that you have to have two selfless people in a situation like this, and I think we have that."He also pointed to something deeper. "Her path to being a professional athlete and being one of the best soccer players in the world hasn't been easy and she's dealt with more adversity than me," Shelton said. "To see that, understand it with the unfiltered version of it has been eye opening for sure. It puts perspective on things in life and is just cool to see her make it to where she wanted to."Rodman missed significant time in 2025 with chronic back pain, going on indefinite medical leave before fighting her way back to the pitch. Shelton had a front-row seat for all of it. "It was tough to watch last year, her being in pain, just doing everyday stuff, living life and not even taking soccer into account," he said. Watching someone you care about grind through pain with no finish line in sight changes how you see your own bad days on court. Shelton has said as much.She has not been subtle about it. Rodman wore a T-shirt reading "I ♥️ MY BOYFRIEND" during Shelton's second-round match at the 2026 US Open. She has also shown up to smaller ATP events that most partners skip entirely. Unlike many who only attend Grand Slams, Rodman supported Shelton at ATP events in Stuttgart and Dallas in the lead-up to the US Open.Then there was the press conference moment. After a Washington Spirit match in September 2025, Shelton picked up a microphone and started interviewing Rodman himself. She reportedly could not stop laughing. It was the kind of thing that does not need any explanation. He showed up, made her laugh, and went home."It's funny because she's really gotten into tennis the way that I've gotten into soccer," Shelton said. "She's watching it all the time. Sometimes I'll go home, and she will have YouTube on, watching one of my old matches." That detail probably says more about where they are than any post-match interview.Most high-profile athlete relationships exist largely in public-facing moments: the courtside appearances, the Instagram posts, the post-match mentions. Shelton and Rodman have all of that. But the more specific moments, the 5am arrivals, the press conference interviews, the immediate appearance at her NWSL game after Wimbledon ended early, point to something that functions differently in practice.Both of them understand the specific weight of competing under national expectation. Shelton is trying to become the first American man to win a Grand Slam since Andy Roddick in 2003. Rodman is one of the most scrutinised players in women's soccer, carrying both her own ambitions and the considerable weight of her famous surname. They are not just supporting each other. They are watching each other carry real pressure, up close, and choosing to stay present anyway.That, more than the matching custom outfits or the fire emoji origin story, is what makes this particular sports relationship worth paying attention to.
Article Summary: Ben Shelton and Trinity Rodman have been dating since March 2025. Rodman plays for the Washington Spirit in the NWSL and represents the US Women's National Team. Shelton is in the US Open semi-finals and is ranked No. 9 in the world.

Article Title: "It's going to be challenging": Max Verstappen reveals his surprising plan for a crazy 100-driver challenge at Silverstone
Article Text:
Max Verstappen is ready for a wild 100-driver challenge at Silverstone (Image via Getty)

Max Verstappen plans to simply show up and race 100 drivers without doing any special preparation

Charles Leclerc warns Max Verstappen about the huge field while Carlos Sainz expects him to reach the front with ease

Max Verstappen is preparing for one of the most unusual racing challenges of his career, and his approach could not be more relaxed. The four-time Formula 1 champion will start from the back of a 100-driver karting field at Silverstone and try to overtake every competitor within 30 laps. The event will bring together athletes, streamers, content creators, personalities and fans, creating a very different racing environment from a Formula 1 Grand Prix. While many drivers might study their rivals before such a challenge, Max Verstappen has chosen not to. Instead, he plans to arrive, race and deal with whatever happens on the track.The biggest surprise surrounding Max Verstappen's Silverstone challenge is not only the number of competitors. It is how little preparation he has done for the event.A normal Formula 1 weekend gives drivers plenty of information before they race. Teams study opponents, analyze track data and prepare for different situations. Max Verstappen will have none of that same structure when he lines up behind 100 go-karters.The Dutch driver admitted that he has not researched the people he will face."No, I didn't do anything," Max Verstappen said when asked if he had looked up his competitors.Max Verstappen then made it clear that he intends to treat the event as something to enjoy rather than another highly controlled race weekend."I'll just rock up and have a good time, to be honest. Let's see how it goes. But yeah, it's a lot of people."That relaxed attitude does not mean the challenge will be simple. Starting at the back means Max Verstappen will have to work through traffic almost immediately. With 100 karts sharing the circuit, finding clean space and choosing the right moment to pass could become a major part of the test.Max Verstappen also does not yet know exactly how the event will work."Starting from the back, it's going to be challenging, but I hope I can catch them all. But we don't know yet. I don't even know the format at the moment. So I will just rock up and do my thing."For a driver known for his aggressive racecraft and quick decisions, the event could become a test of instinct more than preparation.Max Verstappen's Formula 1 rivals have already offered their thoughts on the unusual challenge, with Charles Leclerc focusing on the risks created by such a large field."I mean, 100 is a lot," Charles Leclerc said.The Ferrari driver joked that competitors should avoid crashing into Max Verstappen, especially because the Red Bull Racing driver still has a Formula 1 season to finish. Charles Leclerc also questioned how experienced some of the participants might be compared with a professional Formula 1 driver.Carlos Sainz was even more confident about Max Verstappen's chances.Carlos Sainz recently competed in a karting race where he started 20th because of a reverse-grid format. He said he reached first place within five laps, giving him a simple way to estimate how quickly Max Verstappen could move through the Silverstone field."I did a karting race yesterday with my team. Started 20th because we did reverse grid and I was P1 in five laps. So by my calculations, if there are another 20 times five, in 20 laps Max will be P1 for sure. 15-20 laps, or who knows, depends how much overtaking there is. But he will win it easy."Carlos Sainz's prediction adds confidence to the idea that Max Verstappen could reach the front well before the 30-lap limit. Still, the 100-driver field introduces an element of uncertainty that cannot be measured through normal Formula 1 experience.For Max Verstappen, that appears to be exactly what makes the event interesting. He will have speed and experience on his side, but the crowded track, unknown competitors and unusual format could make the challenge unlike anything he faces during a Formula 1 weekend.

Article Title: Sami Zayn wins Undisputed WWE Championship as CM Punk baffled by dirty play in chaotic SmackDown Mexico City
Article Text:

Sami Zayn is the new Undisputed WWE Champion

How Sami Zayn defeated CM Punk

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Sami Zayn is WWE Champion again. However, he didn't get there clean. Friday night's SmackDown was the promotion's first trip to Mexico City in 15 years, and the crowd at Arena CDMX got a main event soaked in chaos, interference, and one badly hurt knee.By the time the dust settled, CM Punk was on his back, three other superstars had gotten involved, and Zayn was celebrating his second Undisputed WWE Championship of the year. It wasn't pretty, but it didn't look like an accident.Sami Zayn had been chasing this moment since July, when he lost the title after a run that lasted just nine days. He spent the months after insisting he'd been "robbed," and he made it clear he wouldn't stop until he got the belt back.He got his shot Friday night, in the main event of a card already stacked with four title matches. And when the opportunity was on the table, Zayn didn't hesitate to take the ugly route. Once CM Punk showed signs of a knee injury early in the bout, Zayn went straight after it, working the leg with a focus that bordered on ruthless.Punk opened strong, backing Zayn into the corner with right hands before adding a second-rope strike and a suicide dive to the outside.But the tide turned fast. Zayn slammed Punk's knee into the ring post, then locked in a Figure-Four leg lock, forcing Punk to scramble for the ropes.Punk kept fighting through it. He tried to answer with a GTS, but his leg buckled under him. Zayn, working through an injured wrist of his own, needed two attempts to land the Blue Thunder Bomb, and Punk kicked out of both. Punk then found the Anaconda Vice, and for a moment it looked like Zayn might tap. The referee, though, was looking the other way.That's when things spiraled. Johnny Gargano and Candice LeRae showed up ringside, and while LeRae pulled the referee's attention, Gargano grabbed the title belt and went after Punk. Punk answered with a GTS instead, dropping Gargano and sending the belt to the mat. Just as Zayn reached for it, Kevin Owens came out of nowhere, scooped it up, and swung at Zayn. Zayn ducked, and unfortunately Owens hit Punk.Zayn wasted no time after that. He hit Owens with a low blow, tossed the belt outside, and dropped Punk with a Helluva Kick. The three-count made him champion again.Zayn's celebration filled the arena as SmackDown went off the air, but the manner of the win is already drawing plenty of debate. With Owens, Punk, Finn Balor, and Gunther all still circling the title picture, Zayn's second reign is starting under just as much scrutiny as his first one ended.
Article Summary: Sami Zayn is the new Undisputed WWE Champion. He beat CM Punk in a main event soaked in chaos, interference, and one badly hurt knee. Zayn had been chasing this moment since July, when he lost the title after a run that lasted nine days.

Article Title: Sophie Cunningham drops candid reaction to ‘s*x symbol’ perception around her name: “That is way better”
Article Text:

Sophie Cunningham reacts to 's*x symbol' perception

Sophie Cunningham launches new podcast

Sophie Cunningham has never appeared interested in fitting the usual image of a WNBA player. The Indiana Fever guard has been open about her personality, her fashion choices, and her willingness to answer difficult questions without much hesitation. During a recent conversation with Colin Cowherd, Cunningham found herself facing a label that often follows athletes who attract attention outside the court. Her reaction was not defensive. Instead, she laughed it off and made it clear she was comfortable with how she presents herself.During an appearance on Colin Cowherd's Volume podcast network, Sophie Cunningham was asked about how she is viewed within the WNBA. Cowherd began describing her place in the league before pausing. "You are kind of viewed as the leagues…ummm," Cowherd hesitated."Just say it," Cunningham interrupted."S*x symbol," he responded."That is way better, I thought you were gonna go somewhere completely different," she responded jokingly.Cunningham later explained why she has no problem embracing a more feminine image while playing professional basketball.For her, fashion and competitiveness have never been mutually exclusive."For me, the reason why I really lean into that is, first of all, I've always been super girly. Since a little girl, I've always loved to dress up. I love dresses. I love high heels. I love all of that," Cunningham explained.The Fever guard continued, "For some reason, our society, if you play basketball, you can't dress that way, or you can't be girly. No one's ever said it, but it's like, they kind of feel like you can't be both. Screw all that. Yes, you can. You can be girly, and you can go out and kick someone's a*s."Cunningham has also added another outlet for those conversations with the launch of "No Hesitation," a podcast she hosts with basketball trainer Drew Hanlen. The show debuted Thursday and replaces "Show Me Something," her previous podcast with West Wilson.The new program is centered on basketball and the personalities surrounding the sport. Cunningham said she wanted a platform where conversations could be more direct."I just felt like there was not a podcast or really any social media out there that gave you real, honest truth about basketball and strictly basketball," Cunningham said.Hanlen also addressed the gap between Cunningham's actual comments and the way some of them are portrayed online."People think you’re like some troll and make statements, but really it’s 99% of the time people ask you a question, you answer, you give your opinion, and then people blow it up and act like you made a big political statement," Hanlen said."Stop asking me questions if you don’t want the truth," Cunningham responded.Cunningham used the debut episode to discuss several basketball-related topics, including media coverage and recognition within the WNBA. She argued that popularity and politics can sometimes influence award voting."I think it’s very political. I think there’s a lot of people who are really, really great who don’t get the credit because maybe they don’t have the popularity or they don’t have the platform," Cunningham said.She also called on the league's media to focus more closely on what is happening on the court."I think you kind of hit it when you said the WNBA media pretty much covers everything but basketball," Cunningham said.Cunningham believes the league is entering an important period, with the WNBA expanding and a new commissioner set to take over after Cathy Engelbert's planned departure at the end of 2026. She said better practice facilities should be a basic priority for every franchise.The podcast is scheduled to release new episodes each Thursday, with Cunningham promising a mix of film study, strategy and candid discussion around professional basketball.

India's search for consistency in T20I cricket will continue with a three-match series against Afghanistan, but the team's batting combination could once again come under scrutiny, particularly with vice-captain Tilak Varma's role yet to appear fully settled.India, led by Shreyas Iyer, endured a difficult run following their second consecutive T20 World Cup triumph earlier this year. The team lost all six of its T20Is against Ireland and England before finally putting together a 3-0 clean sweep against Zimbabwe.The Afghanistan series begins on September 13 (Saturday), with India also scheduled to play a historic T20I against Japan before featuring in the Asian Games 2026.With several established batters competing for places, former South Africa star AB de Villiers believes India could face a selection headache, particularly when it comes to deciding where Tilak Varma fits into the batting order.Speaking on his YouTube channel, de Villiers pointed to the number of batting options available to India and questioned how the team would accommodate its vice-captain."There will definitely be some selection issues with regard to the batters.Obviously, Shreyas, captain, Ishan Kishan, Samson, Sooryavanshi, and then there are all-rounders, Tilak Varma; I think that’s where the balance is quite tricky. Where will he bat?" de Villiers said.Tilak's recent numbers also underline why his position could become a talking point.Since the 2026 T20 World Cup, the left-hander has scored 255 runs from 10 innings at a strike rate of 159.36, with three scores of 50 or more. However, the numbers need some context. One of those half-centuries came during the recent Zimbabwe series, while another was scored in the fifth T20I against England, by which point India had already conceded the series.His overall returns therefore look stronger in isolation than his performances across the entire period suggest. Tilak endured a particularly difficult run during India's tour of the UK, and his inconsistency has remained a concern despite the occasional big score. That makes his position in India's batting order an even bigger talking point ahead of the Afghanistan series.The presence of Shreyas Iyer, Ishan Kishan, Sanju Samson, Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi gives India several batting options, while the team also has to factor in its all-rounders.For de Villiers, the challenge is not simply about selecting the strongest players but finding a combination in which every batter has a clearly defined role.He believes India have enough quality in their squad to deal with Afghanistan, but stressed that clarity will be particularly important against a side he considers dangerous."Really, really strong squad, but the balance will be tricky to figure out. It is T20 cricket, so they can play around with the squad a little bit. There are different roles, but the role clarification will still be incredibly important for India, as they are playing quite a dangerous team," de Villiers stated.The Afghanistan series marks the next stage of India's T20I campaign after their contrasting results against Ireland, England and Zimbabwe.Under Iyer, India will now look to build greater stability in the format, with the batting order likely to be one of the key areas under the spotlight.The three-match series against Afghanistan starts on September 13, before India take on Japan in a historic T20I and then turn their attention to the Asian Games 2026.
Article Summary: AB de Villiers questions Tilak Varma's role in India's T20I team. India face Afghanistan in a three-match series starting on September 13. World Championships next, Olympics beyond

For the first time since she began her education, Harita Bhadra gave herself a year without having to divide her attention between studies and athletics.Last year, she graduated from Loughborough University in the UK with a BSc in Sports Science, Coaching and Physical Education. This year, she decided to focus only on athletics.The decision has already produced the most productive season of her career.A national indoor 60m title, multiple personal bests, a national 200m title, Asian Games qualification and now an 11.22-second 100m run have followed.The latest one took a moment to sink in.Bhadra had just won the 100m final at the Indian Athletics Series Final in New Delhi on Thursday. The clock showed 11.22 seconds, another personal best and the second-fastest time ever by an Indian woman in the event.She looked stunned. Then Unnathi Bollanda, who had finished fourth, came over and hugged her as Bhadra celebrated.The two will be teammates again at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya. Both will compete in the 200m and 4x100m relay.“I was just very happy. Obviously, I’m very happy to have come away with a PB,” Bhadra told Timesofindia.com.The Asian Games will be the 23-year-old’s first international competition.She earned her place in the 200m after winning the event at the National Inter-State Athletics Championships in Bhubaneswar in June. Her 23.14 seconds was inside the Asian Games qualification standard of 23.70 and moved her to ninth on India's all-time list.Bhadra had already dipped below the qualifying mark in the heats, running 23.55.Her 200m form had been building through the season. In June, she ran 23.58 at Indian Series-10, at the time a lifetime best. Earlier, she had won the national indoor 60m title in 7.32 seconds.She will now take that form to the Asian Games as part of India's athletics contingent.“I’m very excited to do the 200 because this will be like my first international event ever,” she said. “So I’m excited to represent India and do my best and get a medal for India.”When asked what a successful Asian Games would look like, she kept the answer simple.“Definitely being on the podium and getting a personal best.”The decision to make athletics the priority this year came after years of being a student-athlete.“I’ve been tackling studies and sports since I started my education,” she said. “Last year, I graduated. I did a BSc in Sports Science Coaching and Physical Education from Loughborough University in the UK.”She wanted to see what a full year of training would bring.“And this year, I decided to give myself to athletics so that I can only focus on training because I’ve been a student-athlete since I started my education,” she said. “So I wanted to give this year to myself.”Her sprinting started at Udayachal High School in Vikhroli, Mumbai. There were races at the school sports day. Her PE teacher suggested she join athletics, and the school also had athletics training.“So it started from school,” Bhadra said. She began competing at under-12 level. The shift in ambition came a few years later.“I think it was serious from like under 16,” she remembered. “I started [at] under 12, but from under 16, I was like, that’s I want to, you know, reach [the level] till like represent India and win medals for India.”Her family never made winning a condition.“I have never received any sort of a pressure from them that you should win, you should win or you’re not doing well or anything,” she said. “They have always supported me and they just want me to do my best, be happy.”That has allowed her to enjoy the sport without feeling that every race comes with an expectation to win.“It is because of this environment I get that I can also perform and, you know, be like enjoy and do the sport, not in a pressure sort of a way.”Bhadra has also found a different training environment over the last year.“It has been one year since I’ve joined Reliance Foundation. So definitely it has helped me so much.” she said.“And in that one year, I can see the progress I have made. It’s a collective progress of not just one year because I’ve been training for past years as well.“This is like my first time travelling with the team. So like, I don’t feel the short, like I feel like I have my family over here,” she said.“If I need anything, I have coaches, I have physios, I have a nutritionist, I have anybody to talk to. Plus the teammates as well.”Training alongside national and international athletes has also changed her daily routine.“Training with national athletes, international athletes in itself is like, okay, you have to push as well,” she said.“When you’re just regular day in training, you see the national athletes and everybody. So that definitely pushes you because you want to achieve that as well.”Plenty is going on in Bhadra's life outside the track too.She has a handmade jewellery brand called Dagina. She designs and makes the jewellery herself and sells it online.“So I myself have designed and made jewellery and sell it online,” she said.Bhadra talks about personality when asked about the sportsperson she admires most.Her idol is Rafael Nadal.“I just love his personality because mentally he’s so strong, but outside court he’s also such a good human,” Bhadra said.“He carries himself with so much humility and, you know, like, I don’t know the right word for it, but he’s been my idol. Like, that’s how I want to be.”She also admires Nadal's respect for everybody and what she describes as a healthy rivalry.For Bhadra, the next target after the Asian Games is the World Championships next season.“Obviously it is the Asian Games for this season, but next season, the goal is the World Championship because I want to represent India for the Worlds,” she said.And the long-term target is clear.“Like everybody, an Olympic medal.”But Bhadra does not want to spend too much time thinking that far ahead.“My life mantra would be one day at a time,” she said. “Like I would only think about one day at a time. I don’t want to think so far ahead.”“But we will think step by step. I don’t want to think, and because thinking so far, I think for me is just adding pressure, unnecessary pressure.”“So you should just, like, my life mantra would be one day at a time.”
Article Summary: Harita Bhadra will compete in the 200m and 4x100m relay at the Asian Games. The 23-year-old ran a personal best of 11.22 seconds to win the 100m final in New Delhi. She also won the national indoor 60m title in 7.32 seconds. The Asian Games will be her first international competition.

Article Title: Ben Shelton reaches US Open final, one win away from ending America’s 22-year wait
Article Text:
Ben Shelton, of the United States (AP Photo)

Shelton survives another demanding stretch

Tiafoe's semifinal jinx continues

Shelton's serve changes the contest

Star-studded crowd watches American showdown

Zverev stands between Shelton and history

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Ben Shelton is one victory away from ending the United States' long wait for a men's Grand Slam champion after winning an all-American US Open semifinal against Frances Tiafoe on Friday.The No. 8 seed recovered from losing the opening set to beat Tiafoe 4-6, 6-3, 6-3, 7-5 and book his place in his first major final.Shelton will face top seed Alexander Zverev in Sunday's championship match, with the German having earlier defeated Karen Khachanov 6-3, 7-6 (7), 7-6 (6).A victory over French Open champion Zverev would give the United States its first men's Grand Slam champion since Andy Roddick won the US Open in 2003."I'm going for it here, and I'm going to leave it all on the court," Shelton said. "I hope you guys come and back me. Let's do it for the USA."Zverev, meanwhile, is looking to add a second major title this year after finally breaking his Grand Slam drought at the French Open."Hopefully I can not make the American dream come true on Sunday," Zverev said.Shelton's run to the final has come despite an exhausting schedule.The 23-year-old from Georgia defeated defending champion Carlos Alcaraz in a quarterfinal that finished at 3:33 a.m.on Wednesday, the latest ending to a match in US Open history.Yet Shelton showed no signs of running out of energy against Tiafoe.The two Americans had both needed match tiebreakers in their respective quarterfinals, but Shelton produced the stronger finish when it mattered most."This is where we want to be: at the tail end of this tournament," Shelton said. "This is both of our favorite tournament in the world, our favorite court in the world and to be able to light it up in front of (this crowd) is the best feeling that there is."Shelton was less than a year old when Roddick won his US Open title. Now, more than two decades later, he has a chance to become the American who finally brings the men's Grand Slam trophy back home.Tiafoe's latest US Open campaign ended with another semifinal defeat.The American is now 0-3 in US Open semifinals, with each of his last two losses coming against compatriots. Taylor Fritz defeated him in 2024 before going on to lose the final to Jannik Sinner.Tiafoe had also produced one of the tournament's most dramatic comebacks in the quarterfinals, recovering from two sets down before overcoming fellow American Alex Michelsen after erasing a 3-0 deficit in the deciding set.He began the semifinal as the cleaner player. After a ceremony commemorating the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks, which featured a giant American flag unfurled across the court, Tiafoe made only three unforced errors in the opening set compared with 14 from Shelton.Shelton's double fault at 4-4 handed Tiafoe the break, and the latter closed out the opening set.But the momentum shifted quickly.Shelton responded by increasing the power on his serve and eventually finished the match with 20 aces.At 3-3 in the second set, serving with new balls, he opened with a 125 mph delivery. Tiafoe managed to get his racket to the ball almost in self-defense but was knocked backwards onto the court.Shelton then followed with serves measured at 144, 139 and 140 mph. The final two produced aces and helped him establish control of the set.The third set featured another major test.Tiafoe fought desperately to hold serve in the final game, but the battle lasted 15 minutes and 20 points before he sent a forehand into the net. Shelton took the set and moved within one of reaching the final.The eighth seed then completed the job in the fourth, closing out the match 7-5.The semifinal attracted a high-profile crowd, with sports and entertainment stars turning up for the all-American contest.Serena Williams, Jalen Brunson and US soccer player Trinity Rodman, Shelton's girlfriend, were among those in attendance, alongside actors Salma Hayek, Ben Stiller and Rami Malek.The atmosphere reflected the significance of the occasion, with both Shelton and Tiafoe attempting to become the latest American man to reach a Grand Slam final.Only Shelton managed to take the next step.Standing in Shelton's way is a player who knows exactly what it means to wait for a first major.Zverev had long been regarded as the best men's player without a Grand Slam title before finally winning the French Open this year. He then reached the Wimbledon final, where he lost to Jannik Sinner.The German has gone 24-2 in Grand Slam matches this season and is now back in another major final."Sometimes just things go your way and I feel like I’ve had a lot of struggles at the major level, I was so close so many times, and maybe this year God has said that this is going to be your year and just enjoy the time on the court," Zverev said.Sunday's final will also give Zverev another chance to erase one of the most painful memories of his career.In the 2020 US Open final, he won the first two sets against Dominic Thiem but eventually lost in a fifth-set tiebreak. Thiem became the first man since 1949 to win the US Open after dropping the opening two sets.Zverev has been far more composed after taking early leads this year. He has now won 13 consecutive sets after becoming the first No. 1-seeded man to play five-set matches in each of the first two rounds of a major.Now, Shelton stands between him and another Grand Slam trophy, while the American has the chance to do something no US men's player has managed since Roddick in 2003.
Article Summary: Ben Shelton beats Frances Tiafoe in straight sets to reach US Open final. Shelton will face top seed Alexander Zverev in Sunday's championship match. A Shelton win would give the United States its first men's Grand Slam champion since 2003.

Bengaluru: Two-time champions Triveni Continental Kings, who featured in the finals of all the three previous editions of the Global Chess League (GCL), crashed out of the fourth edition on Friday. They remained at the bottom of the standings in the six-team league.Led by Alireza Firouzja, the youngest player to reach Elo rating of 2800 in 2021, the Kings were expected to put up another spirited fight but they lost their way early in the Garden City.
