India's next Test assignment will take them to New Zealand for a two-match series beginning November 19, and former Kiwi fast bowler Trent Boult believes KL Rahul will be one of the Indian batters worth watching closely.The two Tests will form part of India's marathon New Zealand tour, which begins on October 22 and features 12 matches across the three formats. With India needing a strong result to remain in contention for the World Test Championship (WTC) final, the spotlight is expected to fall on several key players, including captain Shubman Gill and pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah .Boult, however, has picked Rahul and his opening partner Yashasvi Jaiswal as the two Indian batters he is particularly looking forward to seeing in action."I'm always a big fan of KL Rahul and his style of batsmanship. So he's a big player at the top of the order for the Indian side. And yeah, I believe Jaiswal is there as well. Two classy batters to see bat. So yeah, be interesting to see," Boult said in an interview to PTI.The timing of the series could make conditions particularly interesting. Unlike India's previous Test tours of New Zealand, which have often taken place in the February-March window, this series will be played in late October and November.Boult feels the timing could bring colder weather into play, while he is hoping the New Zealand pitches retain some grass and offer assistance to the home attack."It's always an exciting chance when the Indian team comes down to play Test cricket in New Zealand," Boult said."The only thing I can see happening is it's going to be late October. I believe, just coming out of winter. So it's going to be quite cold. Hopefully, there's a bit of greenness in the wickets for some of our bowlers. It's going to be a good series, I'm sure," the star former Kiwi pacer added.Boult also backed the current New Zealand bowling unit to make an impact against India, pointing to the variety available to the team.Kyle Jamieson, Matt Henry, Nathan Smith and Will O'Rourke bring different qualities to the attack, and Boult believes that gives New Zealand enough options to develop its own identity."I think the bowling is very well balanced. Article Title: From teammate to coach, Ishank Jaggi watched Ishan rebuild himself
Article Text:
Coach Ishank Jaggi during the 2026 Jharkhand T20 Cricket League

Kolkata: Almost fourteen years after Ishank Jaggi was named Player of the Match when East Zone last won the Duleep Trophy, he watched Ishan Kishan collect the same award as the region ended its long wait for the title.For Jaggi, the coincidence was nostalgic. But more than the memories of his own playing days, seeing someone he considers a younger brother reach the summit gave him more satisfaction.With their similar names — Ishank and Ishan — adding a little coincidence to a bond that has grown from being teammates to mentor and student, Jaggi has known Kishan since the latter was around 16. He was one of the young wicketkeeper-batter’s first senior teammates and, over the years, their relationship evolved from dressing-room association to a much closer bond. Jaggi later worked with Kishan at his cricket academy and also played a role in his development as a coach.That has given Jaggi a ringside view of Kishan’s journey — from an exciting, aggressive young batter to a more mature all-format cricketer.“Ishan always had that fighting spirit and hunger. That was never missing. What has changed is the experience and maturity he has gained,” Jaggi said.Kishan’s difficult phase after losing his place in the India side and his BCCI central contract in 2024, according to Jaggi, became an important turning point.“Sometimes when you hit rock bottom, you start thinking more deeply about your game and your career,” he said. Rather than allowing the setback to derail him, Kishan used the period to work on several aspects of his game. Jaggi said the batter put considerable effort into his batting, fitness, nutrition and preparation, while also developing a better understanding of his own game.The biggest change, Jaggi believes, has been in Kishan’s ability to temper his natural aggression according to the demands of a situation. “He was always seen as an attacking player, but over the last couple of years he has shown that he can also build an innings and play according to what the team requires,” Jaggi said.His stint with Sunrisers Hyderabad also helped in that evolution. At Mumbai Indians, Kishan had been part of a star-studded batting line-up. With SRH, he was entrusted with greater responsibility as stand-in skipper in Pat Cummins’ absence in the early part of 2026 IPL, something Jaggi feels accelerated his growth.“Responsibility often helps a player grow,” he said.The results have been visible since Kishan began his comeback through domestic grind and then grabbed the opportunities that came his way. His performances eventually took him back into India’s plans, culminating in his return to the national T20 setup.For Jaggi, however, the journey is personal as much as professional.When East Zone reached this year’s Duleep Trophy final, someone tagged Jaggi on social media, reminding him of his own Player of the Match performance in the 2012 final. It was only then that he realised how striking the parallel was.“I hadn’t really thought about it until someone tagged me,” Jaggi said.Jaggi had won the honour when they last lifted the trophy in Oct 2012. Almost fourteen years later, Kishan — the player he has known since his teenage years and later worked with as a coach — produced a match-winning performance in the final and claimed the same individual award.Yet, Jaggi insists he is not living in the past. “I’m more excited about the current team. My playing days are over, so there’s no point living in the past,” he said.Instead, his pride is centred on Kishan and the new generation he has seen emerge from Jharkhand.“More than anything, I’m happy for Ishan. He’s like a younger brother to me.”As Kishan lifted the trophy after leading East Zone to their first Duleep title in 14 editions, Jaggi could look back at the journey from a young player in the dressing room to a cricketer he helped nurture away from the spotlight.“It gives me immense satisfaction,” Jaggi said.For a coach-cum-mentor who had watched the highs and lows from close quarters, seeing Kishan turn adversity into a statement of maturity — and then repeat his own Duleep Trophy Player of the Match feat — made the moment all the more special.
Article Summary: Ishank Jaggi was named Player of the Match when East Zone last won the Duleep Trophy in Oct 2012. He watched Ishan Kishan collect the same award as the region ended its long wait for the title. The coincidence was nostalgic. But more than the memories of his own playing days, seeing someone he considers a younger brother reach the summit gave him more satisfaction.

Article Title: Anthropic researcher who quit over AI safety walked away two months before his stock vested; says: I no longer have anything to gain by…
Article Text:
Jacob Coxon quit Anthropic four months in, two months before his equity vested, saying he no longer had anything to gain from the company's valuation.

Anthropic is heading for one of the biggest IPOs ever, and safety is the sales pitch

Coxon says he never saw Anthropic cut corners. He worries the race will force it.

An Anthropic safety lead replied to the resignation thread and agreed with it

An Anthropic researcher who resigned this week over AI safety fears gave up his entire stake in the company to do it, walking out two months before his equity was due to vest.Jacob Coxon, 27, spent three years doing pretraining research at OpenAI before moving to Anthropic in July. He lasted four months. Staff need six for their stock to vest. His resignation post on X on September 9, now past 130 million views, said neither lab is acting responsibly and that both are "racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives".Axios first reported the forfeited equity, after Coxon told the outlet on Wednesday that "I no longer have anything to gain by juicing up Anthropic's valuation" and that he left before any of his shares vested. He still holds equity in OpenAI, where his work included GPT-4o.The company is preparing a listing at a reported $2 trillion valuation, built in large part on its reputation as the frontier lab that takes risk seriously. That is what gives the equity detail its weight. Researchers have walked out of rival labs over safety before, usually after their stock vested. Coxon left with nothing, then criticised the valuation he could have profited from.He drew that line carefully in the interview. Anthropic's safety work is sincere, he said, and he has not seen it compromised to outpace competitors. What worries him is pressure over time. Race hard enough and you cut corners, or skip steps in the oversight process. He also described a mood he thinks becomes self-fulfilling, calling it excessive paranoia about OpenAI and about China. Colleagues, he wrote earlier, have started using words like "crunchtime" and "endgame".His most quoted line was about where these decisions are being taken. It is insane, he said, that the work happens on the MacBooks of engineers in San Francisco rather than in a bunker in the desert like the Manhattan Project.Evan Hubinger, who runs alignment stress testing at Anthropic, wrote that he personally puts the odds of AI killing all humans above 10 percent within the decade. He said the company is trying, but has no plan yet for aligning superintelligence and is not clearly on track to find one.Coxon's argument is partly about candour. Executives soften their phrasing for the press, he wrote, then say the same things privately, and the belief that AI could kill everyone by the end of the decade is not a marketing stunt. He also described something that used to be a thought experiment. Models now know when they are being tested, and reason about the fact while it is happening.He pointed to the recent run of cyber incidents at frontier labs, including July's Hugging Face breach, as evidence the risk has left the theoretical stage. Coxon is among more than 1,000 researchers who recently signed a statement calling for governments to coordinate on a way to slow AI development if models start improving on their own. Anthropic has not commented on his departure.
Article Summary: Jacob Coxon quit Anthropic four months in, two months before his equity vested, saying he no longer had anything to gain from the company's valuation. Anthropic is heading for one of the biggest IPOs ever, and safety is the sales pitch. Coxon says he never saw Anthropic cut corners. He worries the race will force it.

Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge
Article Text:
El Rubius reacted honestly after his elimination from MrBeast’s $1 million challenge, calling it “unfair” and claiming he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings. His response felt real and balanced, especially after MrBeast’s team later sent him a cake, softening the moment.

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit

El Rubius did not just walk away from MrBeast’s $1 million streamer challenge. He opened up. Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. It was not polished or carefully framed. It felt real, and that is exactly why it caught attention so quickly.The clip and his response have since fueled conversations across the streaming space. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. It went to the mods, the subs, and the non-subs alike."He further added, "I’m happy, of course, though admittedly, it was incredibly tough.I wasn't really a fan of the challenge itself, either. But then again... it was basically a three-against-one situation the entire time. I mean, they were targeting me specifically the whole way through. I kept trying to go after RaKai, but, well, he actually just got eliminated in the end. So, at least justice was served for Abraham. Abraham, if you’re watching this, we were all rooting for you, and standing right there with you."His message carried mixed emotions. There was disappointment, yes, but also pride in how he handled things. Giving away his $50,000 winnings to his community stood out as a gesture that meant more than the result itself.He continued with another honest note, saying, "And in the end, karma finally caught up with that little punk. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. Seriously, thank you for all the support and for just being there."He added, "Every time I asked for something in the chat or whatever it was, you guys were right there. You’re incredible. I’m a little disappointed in myself, personally, mostly for not performing better, but hey, I gave it my all, and we still walked away with $50,000, so we’ve got to look on the bright side. All right, guys, big hugs to all my brothers out there!"Interestingly, the story did not end with frustration. Later that day, Rubius revealed that MrBeast’s team had sent him a cake after his exit. It was a small gesture, but it shifted the mood. It showed that even in a high-pressure challenge, there is still room for respect.In the end, Rubius’ reaction felt honest and grounded. That is what stayed with people.
Article Summary: El Rubius was eliminated from MrBeast's $1 million streamer challenge. He called it "unfair" and said he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings.

NEW DELHI: IPL comes and the demand for tickets and passes go soaring up by the fans. The desperation to get inside the stadium to watch their favourite teams in action in the IPL go high and high. When the tickets get sold out, the demand gets too hig, and the cricket fans even ask for tickets in black. But for a 25-year-old techie the craze for IPL tickets for RCB vs CSK turned too costly and he was duped for a massive Rs. 1.46 lakh.The techie, a resident of B Narayanapura, fell into a trap by a post posted by a fraudster who posed himself as a ticket seller on Instagram.As per a report in Deccan Herald, the techie alleged in a complaint to Mahadevapura Police that an individual claiming to be Sumit Biswal promised he could arrange IPL tickets along with food coupons.As per the techie, Biswal was introduced him as a senior supervisor for ticket counter at M Chinnaswamy Stadium"He asked me to come near the stadium gate number 10, saying someone would deliver the tickets within minutes, and even sent an email confirmation to gain my trust," the complainant told Deccan Herald."Initially, I agreed to buy two tickets for Rs 3,700 each,but he kept asking for more money under various pretexts such as refundable security deposits, additional ID cards and food coupons.Trusting him, I made multiple payments - even using my mother’s bank account after exhausting my own limits—and ended up transferring around Rs 1.46 lakh," he added.Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s incisive spell of 3-41, coming after a marauding batting show from Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal, propelled Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) to a commanding 43-run victory over Chennai Super Kings (CSK) in their IPL 2026 encounter at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium on Sunday.The contest saw RCB’s batting unit dismantle CSK’s attack with relentless hitting, as David’s 70 not out off just 25 balls and Patidar’s unbeaten 48 off only 19 balls provided for the late fireworks after Padikkal’s fluent 50 off 29 balls had set the tone for the daunting total.Their combined effort lifted RCB to a daunting 250/3, thus setting a new record for highest total in IPL 2026. In reply, CSK faltered under scoreboard pressure, with Sarfaraz Khan’s 50 off 24 balls and Prashant Veer’s 43 the lone acts of resistance amid a string of failures from the top order.Bhuvneshwar was at his disciplined best and even crossed the 200-mark in terms of wickets in IPL, with others also chipping in as CSK were bowled out for 207 in 19.4 overs. The comprehensive win also meant RCB have registered four consecutive triumphs over CSK for the first time in the IPL’s history.
Article Summary: A 25-year-old techie fell into a trap by a fraudster who posed himself as a ticket seller on Instagram. Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal's combined effort lifted RCB to a daunting 250/3, thus setting a new record for highest total in IPL 2026.

Article Title: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture
Article Text:
A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Instead of conflict, the exchange highlights shared influence and mutual awareness. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration rather than ownership.

Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends

The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. It is a mere, everyday talk that seems almost novel nowadays, in the age of internet, which is overflowing with content. The scene is easy-going, the tone of the narrative is straightforward, and the characters appear more concerned with conversation than combat.The message that is being addressed is the flow of the conversation. It discusses internet culture, the way people communicate with one another and the place of trends. Rather than bringing out a debate, the encounter towards curiosity. It quietly brings attention to something that a lot of people who use the internet notice but don't often say out loud. People in different communities often have a bigger impact on each other than they think.The conversation begins with a confident and lighthearted comment from one of the trans women present. She says, "You know that trans women are like the OG lip masters, right? We are very talented in the program. Like, I do the peptides, I'm on Zeta." Her tone carries a mix of pride and humor, setting a relaxed vibe at the table.Clavicular responds in a way that keeps the mood steady but adds a different angle.He says, "That is funny because you guys were using a lot of the words in like the South Korean subreddits in like 2014." It’s not confrontational. If anything, it feels like an observation. He points to how certain words and ideas may have traveled across different online spaces over time.Another voice joins in and brings the moment full circle. "Guys, we're like the OGs. I saw a couple of posts about that. We're like copying each other." That line hits in a simple but honest way. It reflects something familiar. Online culture is rarely created in isolation. It grows through sharing, borrowing, and sometimes even unknowingly repeating.That's what makes the clip so powerful. It doesn't want to make a point or win an argument. It only shows a group of people talking, listening, and figuring something out together.This moment feels different in a space where viral content often leads to fights. It reminds people that conversations can be calm, thoughtful, and still important. And sometimes, that honest silence is what makes it work.
Article Summary: A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration.

Article Title: BRICS menus put regional flavours on centre stage
Article Text:
Chefs at luxury hotels across Delhi have put together menus reflecting the diversity of regional cuisines

The menus and experiences are designed keeping in mind the diversity and global appeal of the summit

Many chefs are curating menus that offer both Indian and global flavours

Maa ke haath ka khana

in the spotlight





As the 18th BRICS Summit progresses at Bharat Mandapam, with world leaders and delegates in attendance, chefs across luxury hotels in the city are busy putting together menus that reflect India’s rich culinary traditions. The special menus being curated for delegates spotlight regional cuisines, with millets emerging as a key ingredient.“Our culinary team has curated a special menu that brings together the richness of India’s regional cuisine with carefully crafted international influences,” says Vishal Sharma, General Manager, The LaLiT New Delhi, where delegates and representatives from South Africa, Burundi and the UAE among other countries are expected to stay. “Guests can look forward to Indian favourites such as galouti kebabs and freshly baked tandoor breads, alongside a dedicated millet-forward selection that showcases the versatility and nutritional value of our traditional grains. The menu also features dishes like braised eggplant with miso paste, simmered Chinese cabbage and kidney bean sweet Japanese style with Amber sauce. We wanted to offer delegates an experience that is distinctly Indian, while also celebrating the global spirit of BRICS.”Indigenous ingredients like sattu and bajra also feature prominently in some menus. Karan Thakur, Executive Chef, The Leela Palace New Delhi, informs, “We are curating a special culinary experience that celebrates the diversity of Indian cuisine. The menu highlights ingredients such as sattu and bajra, with millet-based preparations. Our royal Indian cuisine has always been a favourite of our visiting delegations. From carefully sourcing ingredients, to crafting menus and service experiences, every detail is being considered with utmost thought.”Another luxury hotel has come up with a special menu featuring recipes inspired by chefs’ mothers. Anmol Ahluwalia, Area Director - Operations, and General Manager, Taj Mahal, New Delhi, shares, “We will present Tradition to Table, a collection of recipes curated by our chefs and inspired by their earliest culinary mentors, their mothers. Some dishes that feature are nalli nihari with khamiri roti, gucchi pulao, Delhi-6 chicken korma, steamed Chilean Sea Bass with turmeric and lime in banana leaf, wok-tossed prawns with tamarind, chilli and palm sugar, lamb chops with black pepper and chilli. ”
Article Summary: Chefs at luxury hotels across Delhi have put together menus reflecting the diversity of regional cuisines. The menus and experiences are designed keeping in mind the diversity and global appeal of the summit. The Leela Palace New Delhi has curated a special menu that brings together the richness of India’s regional cuisine.

Article Title: Nafisa Joseph suicide case: Bombay HC refuses to discharge ex-fiancé, bizman Gautam Khanduja
Article Text:
Nafisa Joseph (Archive Image/TOI)





MUMBAI: Bombay high court has refused to discharge businessman Gautam Khanduja of abetment to the June 29, 2004 suicide of his fiancée, model and 1997 Miss India Universe winner, Nafisa Joseph (then 26).A week before their marriage scheduled on Aug 7, Khanduja had refused to marry her.“Suffice it to observe that there are sufficient grounds to proceed against the applicant and there are circumstances requiring the trial to proceed,” said Justice Milind Sathaye in the Sept 10 verdict.He dismissed Khanduja’s plea challenging the sessions court’s Aug 24, 2005 order refusing to discharge him under IPC Section 306 (abetment to suicide)According to the prosecution, they met in 2003 and got engaged on May 23, 2004. While Khanduja had told her he had divorced his wife, his mother informed her he had not. Following a fight between them over this, on July 28, Nafisa’s mother came from Bangalore to Mumbai. In the presence of both parents, he refused to marry her stating that she was short-tempered. When asked why he did not submit the document as promised, Khanduja kept quiet.Next day again, he reiterated he would not marry her. Around 6 pm, Nafisa’s friend Poonam Damania visited her at her Andheri residence and found she was depressed due to Khanduja’s refusal to marry her.She declined to see a doctor unless Khanduja accompanied her.Despite repeated calls, Khanduja did not come.Thereafter she went to her bedroom, locked the room and ended her life by hanging herself to the ceiling fan with a dupatta. After the FIR was registered, the chargesheet was filed. Following the magistrate's order issuing process, Khanduja (then 33) moved HC. On Nov 29, 2005 HC stayed the trial.Senior advocate Ashok Mundargi, for Khanduja, argued that the chargesheet did not attribute any act of instigation, threat, coercion, humiliation or intentional aid on his part. Prosecutor Manisha Tidke said the said marriage was fixed and invitation cards distributed. In such circumstance, since he refused to marry her, she felt so humiliated by the fear of disrepute to her and her family that she died by suicide.Justice Sathaye said while considering discharge application, HC cannot go into the merits to assess whether the accused can be convicted. “What is required to be considered is whether a prima facie case has been made out or not and whether the accused is required to be tried or not. A mini trial is certainly not permitted,” he added.However on overall consideration of statements, especially mother and friends, about the proximate situation that led to the suicide, Justice Sathaye said it cannot be said at this stage that ingredients of Section 306 are not made out.He also noted that Khanduja and Nafisa knew each other’s past, including her two broken relationships, “thereby making her sensitive and vulnerable to one more such incident.” “Whether the applicant’s refusal to marry and non-supply of divorce papers proved to be the ‘last straw on the back of the camel’ that broke it, will have to be decided at the time of trial,’’ he added. He continued an earlier interim stay on trial for six weeks on Mundargi’s request.
Article Summary: Bombay high court refuses to discharge businessman Gautam Khanduja of abetment to the June 29, 2004 suicide of his fiancée, model and 1997 Miss India Universe winner, Nafisa Joseph. A week before their marriage scheduled on Aug 7, K handuja had refused to marry her. “There are sufficient grounds to proceed against the applicant and there are circumstances requiring the trial to proceed,” said Justice Milind Sathaye in the Sept 10 verdict.

Article Title: Farmer killed in suspected leopard attack in Shahuwadi
Article Text:
Kolhapur

:





A 50-year-old farmer from Shembavne village in Shahuwadi tehsil was killed in an alleged wild animal attack on Wednesday.Sanjay Dhondiba Pankar’s brother Balu Pankar told police that a leopard attacked him when the siblings had gone to Navladeviwadi around 4pm to bring back the cattle they had left outside the village for grazing. When they were about 1km outside the village, the brothers went in different directions, Balu Pankar said.“Suddenly, a wild animal hiding in the bushes attacked Sanjay,” he told police. Hearing Sanjay’s loud screams, Balu said he went in his direction and found his brother in an injured condition. He got the help of some villagers and they took the injured man to Malkapur Rural Hospital for treatment. But, doctors declared he was brought dead. Sanjay is survived by his wife, two daughters, a son, two brothers and his mother.The body remained at the hospital till late at night as relatives refused to take possession until the forest department announced a compensation for the incident.Balu Pankar said, “We complained to the forest department in the first week of Aug regarding the sighting of a leopard on Malkapur-Anuskura highway. However, the forest department didn’t take any efforts to trap the animal.If they had taken action, today, my brother would have been alive. The forest department should pay compensation and trap the leopard responsible.”Forest department officials were not available for comment at the time of going to press.A team of Pendakhale division’s range forest officer Kishor Aher, forest ranger PN Daphade, and forest guards Sangam Khupse, Suresh Patil, Shivaji Patil, Sakharam Kamble visited the spot and took information about the attack. An inquest was conducted.
Article Summary: Sanjay Dhondiba Pankar, 50, from Shembavne village in Shahuwadi tehsil was killed in an alleged wild animal attack on Wednesday. His brother Balu said a leopard attacked him when the siblings had gone to Navladeviwadi around 4pm to bring back the cattle.

Article Title: Khalapur temple theft: Video shows masked man stealing silver Padukas; 2 arrested in Pune
Article Text:
he accused stole silver Charan Paduka from Shree Swami Samarth temple on September 2





NAVI MUMBAI: The Khalapur police probing the theft case wherein a masked man had decamped with a pair of silver toe-knob sandals (Charan Paduka) representing divine footprints offered at Shree Swami Samarth temple in Khalapur city on September 2, have arrested the acccused thief and his aide by tracking them to Pune on Monday.Pradeep Rayannavar, senior inspector of Khalapur informed that, the arrested accused are Mahendrasingh Rathod, 45, who hails from Rajasthan and Ravi Soni, 32, who hails from UP and is a history-sheeter as a theft case is registered against him in Pune.Both were presently residing in Chikhali, Pune district.On September 2, the temple trustee Deepak Bodarde, 68, lodged a complaint of theft of silver Padukas from the temple.When the CCTV footage of the temple premises was checked, it was seen that a masked man wearing a hat and attired in white Kurta-Payjama entering the temple around 7.30am.He goes to the first floor of the temple where the silver Padukas were kept in front of the idol of Shree Swami Samarth.By pretending to offer prayers, he picked up the Padukas and hid them inside his Kurta and exited the temple.Inspector Rayannavar said," The theft was committed when the temple priest had gone to his room near the temple.Upon checking the CCTV footage of the roads near the temple, it was seen that two masked men on a bike were loitering near the temple and conducted a reece before committing the theft.""Considering the religious sentiments of the devotees, Raigad SP forms a special police team to detect the case at the earliest. Subsequently, the CCTV footage along the escape route of the thieves were scanned. The bike used in the crime did not have a registration number plate," Rayannavar added.He further said, "However, using technical expertise, intelligence inputs and footages of CCTV camera along the highways, the thieves on bike were tracked and apprehended from Chikhali in Pune district. We have seized from them the stolen Padukas and the bike used in the crime. On Monday, the acccused were produced before the Khalapur JMFC court that remanded them to police custody till Friday."
Article Summary: A pair of silver toe-knob sandals (Charan Paduka) representing divine footprints offered at Shree Swami Samarth temple in Khalapur city were stolen on September 2. The accused thief and his aide were arrested by tracking them to Pune on Monday.

Article Title: Cop dies by suicide at Navi Mumbai lodge, names ex-DCP, ACP and head clerk in note alleging harassment
Article Text:
The deceased identified as Pandurang Nimba Patil, a resident of Airoli.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 55-year-old Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) with the Navi Mumbai Police allegedly died by suicide at a lodge in Airoli on Saturday evening.The deceased, identified as Pandurang Nimba Patil, a resident of Airoli, had recorded a video before taking the drastic step and posted it on social media.In the video, he alleged that he was compelled to end his life due to harassment by a former DCP, an ACP, and a head clerk.ASI Patil also left behind a nine-page suicide note accusing former DCP (Headquarters) Sanjay Patil, ACP Girish Thakare, and administrative head clerk Jayu Ahire of driving him to take the extreme step by allegedly harassing him while assigning official duties.ACP (Rabale Division) Rahul Dhas said, "ASI Patil had checked into Sachi Lodging and Boarding on Saturday at 4.40 pm. Around 7.30 pm, when the housekeeping staff went to his room, he did not respond, and the door was locked from inside. The lodge manager opened the door with a master key and found ASI Patil hanging from a ceiling fan hook. The lodge manager informed the Rabale MIDC police. ASI Patil was rushed to NMMC Hospital in Vashi, where he was declared brought dead. Prima facie, an accidental death case will be registered at the Rabale MIDC police station."
Article Summary: Pandurang Nimba Patil, a 55-year-old Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) with the Navi Mumbai Police, allegedly died by suicide at a lodge in Airoli on Saturday evening. He recorded a video before taking the drastic step and posted it on social media. In the video, he alleged that he was compelled to end his life due to harassment by a former DCP, an ACP, and a head clerk.
